newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Tuesday that the U.S. military attack on Iraq was "unilateral and taken without discussion with others".
- A leading member of republican terrorist organisation INLA Hugh Torney and another man were seriously injured in a gun attack in Lurgan, Northern Ireland.

- Lower prices and overcapacity in the world's paper and packaging industry led to Jefferson Smurfit Group reporting a 37 percent drop in pretax profits to 127 million Irish pounds for the first six months of 1996.
- New projects in tele-marketing and pharmaceuticals will create 160 new jobs in Dublin and Offaly.
- Irish oil production company Dana Petroleum said it had completed its first programme of well drilling in Siberia and has upgraded its estimate of probable reserves.
- Negotiations to end the strike at Irish department store chain Dunnes Stores on Tuesday night were adjourned without any apparent progress.
- The Irish Exporters Association has called on the Irish government to extend the State Export Credit insurance scheme to cover political risk in Russia.
- Irish building society EBS on Tuesday postponed an increase in its mortgage interest rates until January 1997.

- Investors who lose money to investment brokers in the future will be compensated to a limit of 90 percent of their investment subject to an upper limit of I6,000 Irish pounds, under a new law being prepared in Brussels.
